title: Environment and reproducibility
subtitle: Import the required libraries and record their versions. Use seed 42 for the split and validation folds, matching the other group notebooks.
code:
import sys, json, time, hashlib, gzip, base64
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import sklearn
import joblib
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, KFold, GridSearchCV, cross_val_predict, GroupKFold
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.multioutput import MultiOutputRegressor
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from sklearn.dummy import DummyRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score, mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, mean_absolute_percentage_error

SEED = 42
np.random.seed(SEED)
versions = {'Python': sys.version.split()[0], 'NumPy': np.__version__,
            'pandas': pd.__version__, 'scikit-learn': sklearn.__version__}
print(json.dumps(versions, indent=2))

title: Load and check the shared dataset
subtitle:
The UCI Energy Efficiency dataset contains 768 simulated designs based on 12 building shapes. The included snapshot preserves the group's shared sheet and row order. Decode it, verify its checksum, and check dimensions, numeric types, missing values and duplicate inputs before modelling.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| x1 | Relative compactness |
| x2 | Surface area |
| x3 | Wall area |
| x4 | Roof area |
| x5 | Overall height |
| x6 | Orientation |
| x7 | Glazing area |
| x8 | Glazing area distribution |
| y1 | Heating load |
| y2 | Cooling load |

Only x1–x8 are predictors; y1 and y2 are targets. Orientation and glazing distribution retain the numeric codes used in the peer notebooks. This imposes an ordering on categories and is a limitation.

Source: Tsanas & Xifara (2012), [Energy Efficiency](https://doi.org/10.24432/C51307), UCI Machine Learning Repository, CC BY 4.0.
code:
DATA_GZIP_BASE64 = ""
data_bytes = gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode(DATA_GZIP_BASE64))
expected_sha256 = '34590f314dde477ce2d521a0a859180e88e8aaf46f46938c393bd384b78a0aa2'
assert hashlib.sha256(data_bytes).hexdigest() == expected_sha256
columns = [f'x{i}' for i in range(1, 9)] + ['y1', 'y2']
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(data_bytes.decode('utf-8')), sep='\t', header=None, names=columns)
assert df.shape == (768, 10), df.shape
assert not df.isna().any().any(), 'Missing values must be investigated.'
assert all(pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[c]) for c in columns)
X = df.iloc[:, :8].copy()
y = df.iloc[:, 8:].copy()
assert not X.duplicated().any(), 'Duplicate feature rows require a grouped split.'
print('Data shape:', df.shape)
print('Missing values:', int(df.isna().sum().sum()))
print('Duplicate feature rows:', int(X.duplicated().sum()))
print('SHA-256:', expected_sha256)
print(df.head().to_string(index=False))
print('\nFeature ranges:')
print(X.agg(['min', 'max']).to_string())

title: Shared held-out split
subtitle:
Reserve 154 designs for testing and 614 for development using an 80/20 split with `random_state=42`. With the same row order, this matches the peer notebooks. Keep the test set out of scaling, tuning and model selection.

This random split evaluates variants within the sampled design space. Section 8 separately checks unseen building shapes.
code:
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED)
assert set(X_train.index).isdisjoint(X_test.index)
assert len(X_train) + len(X_test) == len(df)

print('Test designs:', len(X_test))
print('First five test indices:', X_test.index[:5].tolist())
print('First five actual test targets:\n', y_test.head().to_string(index=False))

title: Define the SVR pipeline
subtitle:
SVR balances a smooth prediction function against penalties for errors outside an epsilon tolerance band. The RBF kernel models nonlinear relationships. **C** controls the error penalty, **gamma** controls the locality of influence, and **epsilon** controls the tolerance.

Fit `StandardScaler` inside the pipeline so each validation fold uses scaling learned only from its training rows. `MultiOutputRegressor` fits a separate SVR for each target.

title: Select parameters using training data only
subtitle:
Compare 36 combinations of C, gamma and epsilon using five-fold cross-validation on the 614 training designs. Select the highest mean R² across the two targets, then refit on the full training partition.

SVR has no epoch-based training curve; the cross-validation table shows the parameter-selection results. The best CV score is a tuning score. The separate held-out test set supplies the final evaluation.
code:
search = GridSearchCV(make_svr(), param_grid, cv=cv, scoring='r2',
                      n_jobs=2, return_train_score=True, error_score='raise')
started = time.perf_counter()
search.fit(X_train, y_train)
tuning_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started
model = search.best_estimator_
print('Best parameters:', search.best_params_)
print(f'Best mean training-partition CV R²: {search.best_score_:.6f}')
print(f'Grid search and refit time: {tuning_seconds:.2f} seconds')
cv_results = pd.DataFrame(search.cv_results_).sort_values('rank_test_score')
print(cv_results[['rank_test_score', 'mean_test_score', 'std_test_score',
                  'mean_train_score', 'params']].head(5).to_string(index=False))

title: Evaluate against a mean-prediction baseline
subtitle:
Report each target separately:
- **R²:** improvement over a mean-value reference; higher is better.
- **MAE:** average absolute error in load units.
- **RMSE:** error in load units with greater weight on large mistakes.
- **MAPE:** average percentage error; both targets are strictly positive.
- **Within ±10%:** proportion of predictions within 10% of the actual load.

Compare against `DummyRegressor`, which predicts the training mean. R² and 100 minus MAPE are not classification accuracy.
code:
started = time.perf_counter()
prediction = model.predict(X_test)
prediction_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started
train_prediction = model.predict(X_train)
baseline = DummyRegressor(strategy='mean').fit(X_train, y_train)
baseline_prediction = baseline.predict(X_test)
assert prediction.shape == y_test.shape
assert np.isfinite(prediction).all()

def regression_results(actual, predicted):
    actual = np.asarray(actual)
    predicted = np.asarray(predicted)
    assert (actual > 0).all()
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'R²': r2_score(actual, predicted, multioutput='raw_values'),
        'MAE': mean_absolute_error(actual, predicted, multioutput='raw_values'),
        'RMSE': np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(actual, predicted, multioutput='raw_values')),
        'MAPE (%)': 100 * mean_absolute_percentage_error(actual, predicted, multioutput='raw_values'),
        'Within ±10% (%)': 100 * (np.abs(predicted-actual) / actual <= 0.10).mean(axis=0)
    }, index=['Heating', 'Cooling'])

results = regression_results(y_test, prediction)
baseline_results = regression_results(y_test, baseline_prediction)
print('SVR held-out test results:\n', results.round(4).to_string())
print('\nMean baseline held-out test results:\n', baseline_results.round(4).to_string())
print('\nTraining R²:', np.round(r2_score(y_train, train_prediction, multioutput='raw_values'), 4))
print(f'Test prediction time ({len(X_test)} designs): {prediction_seconds:.6f} seconds')

title: Inspect errors
subtitle: Plot predictions against actual loads and residuals against actual loads. The diagonal represents perfect predictions; zero residual means no error. List the five largest errors for each target to expose weak cases.
code:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 8))
for i, name in enumerate(['Heating', 'Cooling']):
    actual = y_test.iloc[:, i].to_numpy()
    pred = prediction[:, i]
    lo, hi = min(actual.min(), pred.min()), max(actual.max(), pred.max())
    axes[0, i].scatter(actual, pred, alpha=0.65, s=20)
    axes[0, i].plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], 'k--', label='Perfect prediction')
    axes[0, i].set(title=f'{name}: predicted vs actual', xlabel='Actual load', ylabel='Predicted load')
    axes[0, i].legend()
    axes[1, i].scatter(actual, pred-actual, alpha=0.65, s=20)
    axes[1, i].axhline(0, color='black', linestyle='--')
    axes[1, i].set(title=f'{name}: residuals', xlabel='Actual load', ylabel='Predicted − actual')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

for i, name in enumerate(['Heating', 'Cooling']):
    errors = pd.DataFrame({'actual': y_test.iloc[:, i], 'predicted': prediction[:, i]})
    errors['absolute_error'] = (errors['predicted']-errors['actual']).abs()
    print(f'\n{name}: five largest absolute errors')
    print(errors.nlargest(5, 'absolute_error').round(4).to_string())

title: Building-shape generalisation check
subtitle:
Group by the first five geometric features so each shape stays within one fold. Evaluate only on the training partition, leaving the main test set untouched.

This is exploratory: the parameters were selected using random folds on the same training partition. A definitive unseen-shape comparison would require nested grouped tuning for all models.
code:
shape_groups = pd.factorize(pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(X_train.iloc[:, :5]))[0]
group_cv = GroupKFold(n_splits=5)
group_prediction = cross_val_predict(model, X_train, y_train, groups=shape_groups,
                                     cv=group_cv, n_jobs=2)
grouped_results = regression_results(y_train, group_prediction)
print('Distinct geometries in training partition:', len(np.unique(shape_groups)))
print('Exploratory held-out-shape results on training partition:')
print(grouped_results.round(4).to_string())

title: Prediction function and a small Colab interface
subtitle:
Choose one of the 12 observed geometries, plus orientation and glazing settings. Using complete observed geometries avoids inconsistent combinations of the five shape variables. Apply the fitted pipeline to return both load estimates.

These are simulated-load estimates, not official ratings or guarantees of real-building energy use. Uncertainty intervals have not been calibrated.
code:
geometries = X.iloc[:, :5].drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

def predict_design(shape_index=0, orientation=2, glazing_area=0.1, distribution=1):
    if shape_index not in range(len(geometries)):
        raise ValueError('Choose one of the observed geometries.')
    if orientation not in [2, 3, 4, 5]:
        raise ValueError('Orientation must be a dataset code from 2 to 5.')
    if glazing_area not in [0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4]:
        raise ValueError('Use an observed glazing-area setting.')
    if glazing_area == 0:
        distribution = 0
    elif distribution not in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]:
        raise ValueError('Non-zero glazing requires distribution 1–5.')
    values = geometries.iloc[shape_index].tolist() + [orientation, glazing_area, distribution]
    design = pd.DataFrame([values], columns=X.columns)
    estimate = model.predict(design)[0]
    return pd.Series(estimate, index=['Heating load', 'Cooling load'])

print('Example prediction (observed geometry 0):')
print(predict_design().round(4).to_string())

# Optional widgets are available in standard Colab; the model also works without them.
try:
    import ipywidgets as widgets
    from IPython.display import display, clear_output
    shape_widget = widgets.Dropdown(options=[(f'Geometry {i}', i) for i in range(len(geometries))], description='Geometry')
    orientation_widget = widgets.Dropdown(options=[2, 3, 4, 5], description='Orientation')
    glazing_widget = widgets.Dropdown(options=[0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4], value=0.1, description='Glazing')
    distribution_widget = widgets.Dropdown(options=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5], description='Distribution')
    predict_button = widgets.Button(description='Predict loads')
    prediction_output = widgets.Output()
    def show_prediction(_):
        with prediction_output:
            clear_output()
            print(predict_design(shape_widget.value, orientation_widget.value,
                                 glazing_widget.value, distribution_widget.value).round(3).to_string())
            print('Simulated-load estimate; not an official rating.')
    predict_button.on_click(show_prediction)
    display(widgets.VBox([shape_widget, orientation_widget, glazing_widget,
                         distribution_widget, predict_button, prediction_output]))
except ImportError:
    print('Optional widget packages unavailable here; use predict_design() directly or open in Colab.')

title: Export the fitted model and evaluation evidence
subtitle:
Save the fitted scaler and both regressors together, plus metrics, predictions, CV results and run metadata. Verify that reloading the pipeline reproduces the test predictions. The model remains fitted only on the 614 training designs.

Files are saved in `svr_outputs`, available through Colab's Files sidebar.
code:
output_dir = Path('svr_outputs')
output_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
joblib.dump(model, output_dir / 'svr_pipeline.joblib')
results.to_csv(output_dir / 'svr_test_metrics.csv', index_label='target')
comparison.to_csv(output_dir / 'peer_r2_comparison.csv', index_label='target')
grouped_results.to_csv(output_dir / 'svr_grouped_check.csv', index_label='target')
prediction_table = y_test.rename(columns={'y1':'actual_heating', 'y2':'actual_cooling'}).copy()
prediction_table['predicted_heating'] = prediction[:, 0]
prediction_table['predicted_cooling'] = prediction[:, 1]
prediction_table.to_csv(output_dir / 'svr_test_predictions.csv', index_label='original_row')
cv_results.drop(columns=['params']).to_csv(output_dir / 'svr_cv_results.csv', index=False)
metadata = {'versions': versions, 'seed': SEED, 'test_size': 0.2,
            'train_rows': X_train.index.tolist(), 'test_rows': X_test.index.tolist(),
            'feature_order': list(X.columns), 'dataset_sha256': expected_sha256,
            'selected_parameters': search.best_params_, 'mean_cv_r2': search.best_score_,
            'tuning_seconds': tuning_seconds, 'test_prediction_seconds': prediction_seconds}
(output_dir / 'run_metadata.json').write_text(json.dumps(metadata, indent=2))
reloaded_model = joblib.load(output_dir / 'svr_pipeline.joblib')
assert np.allclose(reloaded_model.predict(X_test), prediction)
print('Saved files:', ', '.join(p.name for p in sorted(output_dir.iterdir())))
print('Saved-pipeline prediction check passed.')
